sec: God created the heavens and the earth in six days and rested on the seventh. Each day ends with “evening and morning” (Genesis 1:1–2:3).
God said “Let there be light”, separated light from darkness, and called them Day and Night.
God made an expanse (firmament) dividing the waters below from the waters above, and called it Heaven (sky).
The waters were gathered into seas and dry land appeared (Earth). God made grass, seed-bearing plants and fruit trees, each after its kind.
God made the sun to rule the day, the moon to rule the night, and the stars, to give light and to mark signs, seasons, days and years.
God filled the waters with sea creatures and the sky with birds, and blessed them to be fruitful and multiply.

God made the land animals, livestock and creeping things. Then He made man in His own image, male and female (1:26-27), gave them rule over the creatures and plants for food, and called everything “very good”.
God finished His work and rested. He blessed the seventh day and made it holy.
Genesis 2:4-25 retells day six in detail: God forms Adam from the dust, plants the garden in Eden and makes Eve. Genesis 3 is the Fall.

Four kings (Chedorlaomer of Elam, Amraphel of Shinar, Arioch of Ellasar, Tidal of Goiim) against the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim and Bela (Zoar). Later Abram with 318 trained men pursued the four kings.
The Valley of Siddim (the Salt Sea) for the first battle; Abram pursued them as far as Dan and Hobah, north of Damascus.
The four kings won the first battle and took Lot and the goods of Sodom. Abram attacked them by night, defeated them and brought back Lot, the people and the goods.
Melchizedek, king of Salem, blessed Abram and Abram gave him a tenth (14:18-20). Abram refused to keep any of the spoil for himself (14:21-24).

e.t: Battle: Egypt and the Red Sea
sec: Pharaoh’s army with chariots against Israel under Moses. Israel did not fight: “The LORD shall fight for you” (14:14).
By the sea near Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal-zephon (14:2).
Israel. They crossed on dry ground; when the Egyptians followed, the sea returned and covered the whole army (14:27-28).
Israel sang the Song of Moses (Exodus 15) and travelled on to Sinai.
Israel led by Joshua against Amalek.
Rephidim, in the wilderness near Sinai.
Israel. While Moses held up his hands on the hilltop, supported by Aaron and Hur, Israel prevailed; Joshua defeated Amalek (17:11-13).
Moses built an altar called Jehovah-nissi. God said He would blot out the memory of Amalek (17:14-16).
Israel under Joshua against the city of Jericho.
Jericho, near the Jordan, the first city taken in Canaan.
Israel. After marching round the city once a day for six days and seven times on the seventh, the people shouted and the wall fell flat (6:20).
Rahab and her family were spared (6:25). Joshua cursed anyone who rebuilt Jericho (6:26). Achan’s secret theft then led to Israel’s defeat at Ai (Joshua 7).
Israel against the men of Ai.
Ai, near Bethel, in the hill country.
First attack: Ai won and 36 Israelites died, because of Achan’s sin (7:5, 7:11). Second attack: Israel won by an ambush set by Joshua; Ai was burned and its king hanged (8:18-29).
Achan was judged (7:25). Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal and read the law to the people (8:30-35).

e.t: Battle: Gibeon and the long day
sec: Five Amorite kings (of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon) against Gibeon; Joshua and Israel came to defend Gibeon.
Gibeon, with the pursuit down the valley of Aijalon and Beth-horon.
Israel. God sent great hailstones, and the sun and moon stood still until the victory was complete (10:11-13).
The five kings were found hiding in a cave at Makkedah and put to death (10:16-27). Joshua then took the southern cities (10:28-43).
Israel under Deborah and Barak against Jabin king of Canaan and his commander Sisera, who had 900 iron chariots.
Mount Tabor and the river Kishon in the plain of Jezreel.
Israel. Sisera’s army was routed; Sisera fled on foot and was killed by Jael with a tent peg (4:21).
Deborah and Barak sang a victory song (Judges 5) and the land had rest for forty years (5:31).
Gideon with 300 men against Midian and its allies, “like grasshoppers for multitude” (7:12).
The valley of Jezreel, by the spring of Harod and the hill of Moreh (7:1).
Israel. The 300 surrounded the camp with trumpets, empty pitchers and torches; the Midianites turned on one another and fled. Oreb and Zeeb were captured (7:25).
Gideon refused to become king (8:22-23). The land had rest for forty years (8:28).
Israel under King Saul against the Philistines. The duel was David against the Philistine giant Goliath of Gath.
The valley of Elah, between Socoh and Azekah (17:1-2).
David. He struck Goliath with a sling stone and killed him with Goliath’s own sword; the Philistines fled and Israel pursued them to Gath and Ekron (17:49-52).
David joined Saul’s household. Saul grew jealous when the women praised David above him (1 Samuel 18).
The Philistines against Israel under King Saul.
The Philistines. Saul’s sons Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchishua were killed, and Saul fell on his own sword (31:2-4).
The people of Jabesh-gilead recovered Saul’s body (31:11-13). David became king of Judah at Hebron (2 Samuel 2:1-4) and later of all Israel.

e.t: War: Jehoshaphat vs Moab and Ammon
sec: Judah under King Jehoshaphat against Moab, Ammon and men from Mount Seir.
The wilderness of Tekoa and the valley of Berachah.
Judah, without fighting. Singers went before the army; the enemy coalition destroyed one another (20:22-24).
Judah collected spoil for three days. The kingdoms around feared God, and Jehoshaphat’s realm had peace (20:29-30).
Assyria under Sennacherib against Judah under King Hezekiah.
The fortified cities of Judah, then the siege of Jerusalem.
Jerusalem was not taken. After Hezekiah prayed, the angel of the LORD killed 185,000 in the Assyrian camp (19:35).
Sennacherib went home to Nineveh and was killed by his sons (19:36-37).
Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar against Judah under King Zedekiah.
Jerusalem, besieged from Zedekiah’s ninth year to his eleventh (25:1-3).
Babylon. The wall was broken, Zedekiah’s sons were killed and he was blinded and taken to Babylon, and the temple and city were burned (25:7-9).
Most of the people were exiled to Babylon. Gedaliah was appointed governor over those left (25:22). The exile lasted about 70 years (Jeremiah 29:10) until Cyrus allowed the return (Ezra 1).
